effect: The lungs joined the controlled breathing apparatus, completing the goal and showing how diaphragm movement and elastic recoil move air.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the chest, lungs and circulation connected, and the explanation clarified inhalation and quiet exhalation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the controlled apparatus to the lungs was most worthwhile because the result explained how diaphragm contraction draws air in and elastic recoil helps it leave.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed attempt to connect the circulation directly to the pleural membranes was confusing: their physical relationship made the choice seem plausible, but the feedback did not explain the required order.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the circulation could not combine with anything yet; inspecting the membranes then revealed that they first joined the rib cage.

arbitrary.text: The required order for adding the pleural membranes felt somewhat arbitrary from the available descriptions, although inspection made the next action clear.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it continues to explain how the assembled systems work together. This chapter's chemical feedback and breathing mechanics made the connections more interesting than assembly alone.
